title: Time Jump: 07:45, Oil 2.5 Miles Down the Kaw

fields.jumpLabel: +60 minutes from the last time jump (06:45)
fields.scenarioTitle: Ditch to Intake: Prairie Line River Crossing Release & Water Intakes
fields.narration: It is now 07:45 Central Daylight Time, two hours after STARTEX. The leading edge of the slick is about two and a half river miles below the crossing and moving at roughly 2.3 miles an hour. The Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks has closed the Mill Ridge boat ramp and the Kaw Valley Fishing Access, and its deputies are turning anglers away. Ironbark's IMT is staffed at Level 2, and the command post is being set up at Mill Ridge Station, milepost 213.1. The EPA Region 7 On-Scene Coordinator and the KDHE state On-Scene Coordinator are ten minutes out. The volume figure has not changed: 2,700 to 3,500 barrels, with 3,100 barrels as the planning figure. It still comes from the SCADA volume balance and is still unverified. Prairie Spill's Topeka trucks are on the road, but the first boom is still due at the ramp around 10:20. Sterling Bluff's plant superintendent started hourly raw-water sampling at 07:30. The Prairie Bend Rural Water District manager has called back and wants to talk to someone. Ironbark's public line has 31 calls waiting, and Prairie 6 News has set up at the Mill Ridge gate. The river is not going to wait for the Unified Command meeting. You have the next few minutes to update your boards and logs and get ready for that meeting.
worldState: Clock: 07:45 CDT. Line shut in since 06:04; Mill Ridge Station (MP 213.1) and Sandhill Valve (MP 215.6) closed since 06:09. No restart.
Leading edge about 2.5 river miles below the MP 214.3 crossing, moving about 2.3 mph (about 2 knots) at about 8,500 cfs.
Volume: 2,700–3,500 bbl medium sour crude, planning figure 3,100 bbl. Basis: SCADA volume balance VB-0620. UNVERIFIED. Not a worst case discharge. Cause unknown.

TRJ-01 (run 07:05) still applies: plover sandbars at miles 6–9, 08:50–11:25; Prairie Bend RWD intake at mile 11, 10:40–12:25; Cottonwood Slough at mile 22, 14:40–18:10; Sterling Bluff WD intake at mile 34, 19:00 Tue to 00:25 Wed. Next scheduled rerun is 13:05 unless the flow changes by more than 15%.
Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks has closed the Mill Ridge boat ramp and the Kaw Valley Fishing Access. Its deputies are turning anglers away.
Ironbark IMT is at Level 2. IC Gordon Iwata, Environmental Unit Leader Cole Whitfield, QI Teresa Holloway. The command post is setting up at Mill Ridge Station.
EPA Region 7 FOSC and KDHE state OSC arrive in about 10 minutes for the first Unified Command meeting.

Prairie Spill Response Cooperative: Topeka crew on the road with 3,000 ft of 18-inch river boom, two skimmers and two boats. First boom at the ramp around 10:20. Status of Wichita and Kansas City (Tier 2) is whatever the players decided.
Sterling Bluff Water Department: hourly raw-water sampling began at 07:30. No decision has been announced on the intake.
Prairie Bend Rural Water District manager has returned the call and is waiting to speak with the Environmental Unit. No decision has been announced on the intake.
Ironbark public line (555-0118): 31 calls in queue. Prairie 6 News crew is set up at the Mill Ridge gate.
fields.facilitatorNote: Give each role about 5 minutes to update status boards and the notification log. Look for the ENVL to log each utility call by the operator actually reached and the time (a clerk's note or a voicemail does not count). Look for the QI/IC to draft objectives in the order of the UC agenda: objectives, resources, trajectory, safety, protection priorities, next period. If players say the boom will 'stop' the oil at the ramp, point out that the oil has already passed it.

instructorNote: This card gets everyone ready for the first Unified Command meeting. Watch whether the QI/IC ranks protection priorities by arrival time, with the plover sandbars and the Prairie Bend RWD intake first, and whether the ENVL brings an updated trajectory and an honest notification log. Also watch that nobody at Ironbark claims they can close the intakes or the ramp, or say whether the water is safe to drink.
